title: Swimming
description: Signature swimming is taught as comfort first and speed second. A new swimmer learns to float, to breathe out slowly underwater, and to glide, before any stroke is named, because a swimmer who trusts the water will learn every stroke faster. Our programme teaches freestyle first, then backstroke for breathing ease, then breaststroke for rest, and butterfly last, as a reward for strong legs and shoulders. Every session ends with a safety drill, such as floating fully clothed or swimming to the side without panic, so the sport always stays tied to the life skill underneath it.

demo.code:
DIST_KM = 1.0
MINUTES = 22.0
print('Signature swimming pace calculator')
pace = MINUTES / DIST_KM
speed = DIST_KM / (MINUTES / 60.0)
print('Distance: %.2f km in %.1f minutes' % (DIST_KM, MINUTES))
print('Pace: %.2f minutes per km' % pace)
print('Average speed: %.2f km per hour' % speed)
demo.expected_output:
Signature swimming pace calculator
Distance: 1.00 km in 22.0 minutes
Pace: 22.00 minutes per km
Average speed: 2.73 km per hour

training: Sessions pair floating and breathing drills, one stroke studied in depth, and a closing safety drill.
techniques: Signature order is freestyle, backstroke, breaststroke, then butterfly, each built from glide, pull, and kick separately.
safety: Every session ends with a safety drill, and open-water practice always uses a buddy and a bright cap.
history: The Signature school follows the sport's Olympic history while teaching swimming first as a life skill.

title: Diving
description: Signature diving is taught from the water up, not from the platform down. A student learns the rip entry from poolside first, then from one metre, and only then from three metres, because a clean entry is the whole point of the sport and a high board cannot fix a poor one. Our coaches teach the hurdle step and the arm swing as a single rhythm, and every dive is filmed or watched from the side so the student can see what the judge sees. Platform diving comes late, and only when entries from lower heights are consistently clean. The hall's praise goes to the diver whose entry makes the least sound.

training: Sessions pair poolside entry drills, hurdle-step rhythm work, low-board dives, and video review from the side.
techniques: Signature basics are the rip entry, the hurdle step, and the arm swing, taught as one rhythm.
safety: Height rises only when entries are clean, coaches supervise all platform work, and divers never dive alone.
history: The Signature school follows the sport's path from gymnastics exhibitions to Olympic competition.

title: Artistic Swimming
description: Signature artistic swimming is taught as music made visible. A student learns the eggbeater kick until it holds them steady without thought, then sculling until movement looks effortless, and only then a short routine, because synchronisation is impossible without those two foundations. Our teams practise counting aloud before they practise to music, so every swimmer knows the beat in their body before the song plays. Lifts are built slowly, with spotters in the water, and breath-holding is trained gradually and never pushed to distress. The hall's praise goes to the team that looks like one swimmer, not eight.

techniques: Signature basics are the eggbeater kick, sculling, and the ballet leg position, taught before any full routine.
safety: Breath-holding is trained gradually and never to distress, lifts use spotters, and coaches watch every underwater sequence.
history: The Signature school follows the sport from water ballet exhibitions to Olympic competition.

title: Open-Water Swimming
description: Signature open-water swimming is taught as navigation before endurance. A student learns to sight every six strokes, to breathe on both sides, and to draft, in a lake with an escort boat, before any long distance is attempted. Our programme builds distance slowly, adding no more than a tenth to the longest swim each week, and cold water is introduced gradually with short swims and warm recovery. Feeding from a pole is practised in training, not first tried in a race, and every swim ends with a roll call on the shore. The hall's rule is that no swim is worth a swimmer: conditions, not pride, decide whether a swim goes ahead.

techniques: Signature basics are sighting every few strokes, bilateral breathing, and drafting behind another swimmer.
safety: Every swim uses an escort boat, bright caps, and a shore roll call, and conditions decide whether a swim goes ahead.
history: The Signature school follows the channel-swimming tradition from Webb's 1875 crossing to the Olympic marathon swim.

title: Rowing
description: Signature rowing is taught as one boat, one movement. A new rower learns the stroke on a machine first, then in a stable training boat, and only then in a racing shell, because balance learned early saves months later. Our coaches teach the legs-first drive with a simple phrase, legs, back, arms, and they film crews from the bank so rowers can see when the boat stops running level. Coxswains are trained as crew members, not passengers: they learn to steer, to call a race plan, and to keep a crew calm in the last 500 metres. The hall's praise goes to the crew whose blades enter and leave the water together.

print('Daily average: %.1f minutes' % (total / len(DAYS)))
print('Longest session: %s (%d minutes)' % (best[0], best[1]))

training: Sessions pair machine technique, stable-boat rowing, racing-shell work, and bank-side video review.
techniques: Signature basics are the legs-back-arms drive, clean blade entry, and feathering on the recovery.
safety: Life jackets are worn in training boats, crews learn capsize recovery, and coaches follow in a launch.
history: The Signature school follows the sport from Thames watermen's races to the Olympic regatta.

title: Canoe Sprint
description: Signature canoe sprint is taught as rotation before speed. A kayaker learns to turn the torso with each stroke while the arms stay long, and a canoeist learns the kneeling position and the J-stroke before any racing, because a boat that wanders wastes every stroke. Our sessions start with technique paddling at low effort, then add short sprints only when the boat runs straight, and video from the bank shows paddlers what their stroke actually looks like. Starts are drilled separately, since a clean first ten strokes decide many sprint races. The hall's praise goes to the paddler whose boat runs straightest, not fastest, in the first month.

title: Kayak Slalom
description: Signature kayak slalom is taught as reading before racing. A student walks the course on foot, names each eddy and current, and paddles it slowly before any timed run, because a gate missed at speed is a gate never learned. Our coaches teach the eddy turn first, then the ferry across current, then the upstream gate, in that order, since each skill rests on the one before it. Timed runs come only when a clean run is possible, and the hall's praise goes to the paddler who finishes clean, even slowly, rather than the paddler who finishes fast with penalties.

title: Sailing
description: Signature sailing is taught as wind reading before boat handling. A new sailor learns to name the wind's direction, to feel a gust before it arrives, and to point the boat at each point of sail, before any racing, because a sailor who cannot read wind cannot trim a sail well. Our programme starts in a small dinghy with an instructor aboard, then moves to single-handed sailing, and only then to racing, where right of way rules are drilled as a game. Capsize recovery is taught in the first week, so no student fears the water their boat sails on. The hall's praise goes to the crew that gains by reading a shift, not by shouting at rivals.

title: Windsurfing
description: Signature windsurfing is taught as balance before speed. A student stands on a large board in light wind, learns to uphaul the sail without rushing, and practises steering by small weight shifts, before any attempt at planing or foiling. Our instructors teach the fall first: how to fall clear of the board and climb back on, so that falling stops being frightening and starts being ordinary. Foiling comes only when a student can sail, tack, and recover confidently on a normal board. The hall's praise goes to the rider who sails smoothly in light wind, because speed without control is only a faster fall.

title: Surfing
description: Signature surfing is taught as ocean reading before wave riding. A student learns to read a set, to spot a rip current, and to paddle through broken waves, before standing up is even attempted, because the ocean decides every session. Our programme starts on a soft board in small waves, teaches the pop-up on the sand first, and keeps the first rides short and straight. Etiquette is taught as safety, not politeness: the surfer nearest the peak has priority, and dropping in on another surfer is treated as endangering them. The hall's praise goes to the surfer who reads the ocean well and rides within it.

title: Paddleboarding
description: Signature paddleboarding is taught as a walk on water. A student learns to stand, to fall, and to climb back on, in that order, before any stroke is refined, because confidence on the board decides everything after it. Our sessions teach the long stroke from the nose of the board, the sweep turn, and the pivot turn, and they finish with a short tour rather than a race, so the sport stays enjoyable. Yoga on the board comes only when balance is reliable, and racing is offered as an option, never as the point. The hall's praise goes to the paddler who tours furthest with the least wasted effort.

history: The Signature school follows paddleboarding from Hawaiian surf instruction to a worldwide touring and racing sport.

title: Water Skiing
description: Signature water skiing is taught as a start before a ride. A student learns the deep-water start on two skis in calm water, with a patient driver and an observer, before any wake crossing is attempted, because a good start decides whether the rest of the run happens at all. Our programme moves from two skis to slalom only when wake crossings are smooth, and jumping comes last, on a small ramp with a coach boat nearby. The observer's job is taught as seriously as the skier's: the flag goes up the moment a skier falls. The hall's praise goes to the skier whose crossings are smooth and quiet, not the skier who sprays the most water.

title: Wakeboarding
description: Signature wakeboarding is taught as edge control before air. A student learns to carve on both edges, to cross the wake smoothly, and to fall away from the board, before any jump is attempted, because a jump from a poor edge is a crash, not a trick. Our programme teaches the wake jump as a progressive edge that builds to the wake, not as a leap, and spins come only when jumps land consistently. Cable parks are used for rail practice once boat basics are solid, and the hall's praise goes to the rider whose landings are quiet and balanced, run after run.

title: Snorkeling
description: Signature snorkeling is taught as quiet watching. A student learns to fit a mask so it seals, to clear it with a small exhale, and to kick gently without splashing, in a pool, before any reef is visited, because a snorkeler who thrashes sees nothing and tires fast. Our guides teach reef manners as safety: no touching coral, no chasing animals, and no standing on the reef, since the reef is both fragile and sharp. Every outing pairs swimmers as buddies who stay in sight of each other, and the hall's praise goes to the snorkeler who spots the most life while disturbing the least.

title: Freediving
description: Signature freediving is taught as relaxation before depth. A student learns breathing and relaxation on land, then static breath-holding in a pool with a buddy, then short dives, and depth comes only when relaxation is reliable, because tension burns oxygen faster than any technique saves it. Our programme teaches equalisation early and gently, and any ear pain ends a dive at once, with no exception. The buddy rule is taught as the sport itself: a Signature freediver never enters the water to dive without a trained buddy watching. The hall's praise goes to the diver whose dive looks calmest, not deepest.

title: Rafting

A crew learns to paddle together on command, to high-side into a wave as one, and to hold on, on flat water, before any rapid is run, because a crew that cannot move together cannot run a rapid safely. Our guides teach the swim position, feet first and on the back, in a pool, and every trip begins with a safety talk and a practice of the commands. Rivers are chosen by the weakest paddler in the crew, not the strongest, and the hall's praise goes to the crew that runs clean and together, not the crew that runs fastest.
